title: SDK Migration Assistant CLI, language codemods, and changelog automation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Create an SDK Migration Assistant CLI plus per-language codemods and an automated changelog pipeline to accelerate v1->v2 upgrades across Python, TypeScript, and Go. The goal is to reduce friction for customers and internal teams by: (1) automatically detecting common breaking changes, (2) applying safe, reviewable codemods for import/constructor/option renames, (3) surfacing streaming ergonomics and retries changes in examples, and (4) producing a changelog composed from PR metadata, deprecation markers, and doc fragments.

Background & Motivation:
- v2 of Redwood SDKs introduces API surface changes (retry semantics, streaming return types, config renames) that can be tedious to migrate at scale.
- Current migration docs are manual and scattered (examples per-language not standardized). Engineering support requests spike during major releases.
- A small assistant + codemods will save customer time and enable predictable upgrades for internal migration tooling/QA.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Migration Assistant CLI (node-based, cross-platform):
   - detect package(s) and language (python/ts/go)
   - run a dry-run linter pass showing proposed edits and affected files
   - produce patch file(s) and an interactive apply/revert flow
   - export a migration report (list of changed AST transforms, potential runtime migration risks)
2) Language codemods (reviewable Git patches):
   - TypeScript: codemods for import path changes, rename of top-level client constructors, and switching streaming API calls from callback/Emitter patterns to async iterators/ResponseStream classes
   - Python: lib2to3-style transformer for renamed kwargs (e.g., retry_policy -> retry), replacing deprecated sync-only wrappers with unified client and 'stream()' async iterator usage examples
   - Go: gofmt-friendly code replacements, update usage of functional options, and compatibility shims for old retry backoff configs
3) Streaming ergonomics guide and examples repo updates:
   - canonical examples per-language showing: best-practice streaming consumption, deterministic teardown on partial streams, and safe re-tries when using streaming endpoints
4) Retries test harness and CI checks:
   - deterministic fault injector for network/timeouts to verify retry policies and idempotency (unit + e2e scenarios)
5) Changelog automation pipeline:
   - GitHub Actions workflow that aggregates PR labels (breaking-change, docs, example, fix), extracts deprecation markers from code (// DEPRECATE, @deprecated), and composes a candidate changelog in markdown for review by release owners

Acceptance criteria:
- CLI validates and produces patches for 95% of common migration patterns identified by customer support tickets and internal audits
- Codemods have unit tests covering AST transforms and round-trip apply/revert behavior
- Streaming examples for all three languages updated and included in the examples repo (examples/sdk-migration)
- CI gate fails PRs that include deprecated API use in examples or new code without migration note labels
- Changelog workflow produces a candidate changelog draft within each release PR and attaches it as a comment

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- We will implement the CLI in Node for broader cross-platform compatibility and to reuse existing TS codemod tooling (jscodeshift/ts-morph). Python codemods will be produced as separate transformers to avoid coupling the python packaging process to Node.
- We will not attempt fully-automated runtime migrations for stateful patterns (customers must review and opt-in). Automated edits are limited to syntactic changes with a conservative fallback for anything annotated as a runtime semantic risk.
- For streaming ergonomics, prefer an idiomatic pattern per language rather than forcing a mono-pattern. The CLI will provide recommendations, not unilateral rewrites.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Codemods accidentally change semantics (e.g., reordering kwargs). Mitigation: Add comprehensive unit tests, dry-run mode by default, require PR review for apply.
- Risk: Changelog automation misses deprecations in vendor forks. Mitigation: allow manual 'deprecation' frontmatter in release PRs and provide an override UI in the release process.
- Risk: New retry defaults could surface latent bugs in downstream systems. Mitigation: ship feature-flagged rollout and provide canary rollout instructions in console release notes.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1 (2026-02-24 -> 2026-03-02): audit existing deprecation patterns, compile migration pattern catalog, prototype CLI scaffold
- Week 2 (2026-03-03 -> 2026-03-09): implement base TypeScript codemods and dry-run reporting; land minimal GitHub Action for changelog aggregation prototype
- Week 3 (2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-16): add Python/Go transformers, add tests, wire up CI checks to fail on deprecated example usage
- Week 4 (2026-03-17 -> 2026-03-24): finalize streaming examples, integrate retries harness, documentation PRs to docs repo, internal playbook for SRE/SEs

Open questions & TODOs:
- Do we create an official migration NPM/PyPI/Go module distribution for the assistant, or provide it as a one-off release artifact? (pro: discoverability; con: maintenance)
- Should the assistant include opt-in automatic commits/PRs against customer repos (we currently favour manual apply + PR generation for safety)?
- Coordinate with SDK maintainers on the canonical deprecation annotation format (e.g., // DEPRECATE v2.0 -> requires a linting spec)

comments: 2026-02-25: Initial spike complete. Found 18 common migration patterns from support tickets and internal SDK audits.
2026-03-02: Prototype CLI can detect packages and run a dry-run showing edits for TypeScript projects. Demoed to SDK team; positive feedback on interactive review flow.

2026-03-07: Design review - decided to keep codemods conservative. Will not rewrite streaming semantics across the board; instead emit recommended edits and examples. Action: add migration-risk tagging in report.
2026-03-10: Added retry fault-injection harness tests for Python; found one weak spot in current default backoff where repeated 429s caused token duplication. Filed follow-up ENG-20568.
2026-03-12: PR #312 updated with tests for ts import transforms; requested review from Priya. Begin writing the changelog workflow that composes release notes from PR labels and in-code markers.
2026-03-14: Security requested explicit KMS key reference removal check for examples to avoid leaking test keys. Added to CI checklist. Marked security_review_required = true.
